text: Git branching is an important part of version control. A branch lets you work on new ideas without changing the main code. Developers often create feature branches to add a new function or fix a problem. When the work is finished, they merge the branch back into the main project. Before merging, teams usually open a pull request so others can review the changes and discuss them. This workflow keeps the project organized and safe. If something goes wrong, you can simply go back to an earlier version. Learning how branches, merging, and pull requests work together will make you a better and more confident developer.
